question:
Spec: 09 06 00 – Schedules for Finishes, 09 90 00 – Paints and Coatings
Question: Paragraph 1.6.3 of Section 09 90 00 of the specifications requires the use of an SSPC QP 1 certified painter. Paragraph 2.3 of Section 09 60 00 of the specifications requires the use of an MPI 163 approved product for this project. MPI 163 is a Water-Based Emulsion, Semi-Gloss (MPI Gloss Level 5) Paint, suitable for both industrial and architectural exterior wood & metal surfaces.
SSPC QP 1 certified painters are certified to perform field coating applications on complex industrial and marine structures such as bridges, offshore drilling platforms, wastewater treatment facilities, and storage tanks. They are typically large metal structures requiring abrasive blast cleaning and spray painting. Additionally, the UFGS 09 90 00 – Paints and Coatings provides guidance for the designer, stating, “Use bracket option below concerning SSPC QR 1 only when industrial coatings are required”.
The painting work on this project does not seem to fall within the category of structures typically reserved for the requirements of SSPC QP 1. Additionally, This requirement will prohibit local experienced, small business painting subcontractors from being able to perform the work and will result in a substantial increase in the cost of this work, which will be reflected in the prime contractors’ bids submitted to the Government.
Based on the explanations provided above, will the Government please remove the requirement for the use of SSPC QP 1 certified painting contractors from the specifications for this project?
response: Concur, will strike the requirement for SSPC QP 1.

question:
1. Discipline: Contracting
Sheet:
Detail:
Spec: Standard Form 1442
Question: The solicitation indicates that the bids are due to 2:00 p.m. on Monday, 28 September 2026.
We respectfully request that the Government consider shifting the bid due date to another business day.
A Monday morning bid due date significantly limits the contractor’s ability to finalize bids after the close of business on the preceding day, as during the weekend, subcontractors, suppliers, and other key personnel are generally unavailable to respond to last-minute questions, provide clarifications, resolve discrepancies, and submit revised pricing.
In addition, many subcontractors and suppliers routinely submit their final quotes on the last business day before the bid due date. A Monday morning bid due date essentially eliminates the opportunity for meaningful review, coordination, and confirmation of those quotes before submitting the bids.
Providing a bid due date on another business day would allow the contractors to complete appropriate and thorough review, improve the accuracy and completeness of the bids, and encourage greater competition, ultimately benefiting the Government through more competitive pricing.
response:
The Government has evaluated the request to shift the bid due date. Due to strict fiscal year-end funding availability constraints, the deadline cannot be extended beyond the end of the fiscal year.
To maximize competition and accommodate contractor coordination needs as much as possible, the Government is granting a partial extension. The bid due date is hereby shifted from Monday, 28 September 2026, to Wednesday, 30 September 2026 at 2:00 PM EDT.
This change is officially incorporated into the solicitation under Amendment 0004. Offerors must acknowledge this amendment in their proposals.

Several of the performance specifications in this solicitation - including the pad-mounted transformer (Section 26 12 19), switchboard/microgrid controller (Sections 26 24 13 and 26 37 13), engine-generators (Section 26 32 15), and battery energy storage system (Section 48 18 00) - contain detailed performance parameters (e.g., impedance, sound levels, efficiencies, dimensions, and control functionality) consistent with a specific manufacturer’s standard product line. To ensure our sourcing and pricing reflect equipment that will be found compliant, please identify the basis-of-design manufacturer(s) and model(s), if any, used to develop these specifications, or confirm that no single manufacturer’s product was used as the basis of design and that any product meeting the stated performance criteria will be accepted.
response: Microgrid Microgrid: Schneider Electric: C&I Microgrid Flex ECC NG | Generator Cummins C500N6B | PV Modules: Mission Solar Energy P-PERC Bifacial 144HC 550W. | Inverter: CPS SCH100/125KTL-DO/US-600. | Combiner: SMA String-Combiner.

question:
RFI-10: Buy American / Trade Agreements Act Applicability
Section 00 45 00 lists DFARS 252.225-7020, Trade Agreements Certificate, and DFARS 252.225-7000, Buy American-Balance of Payments Program Certificate, as certifications applicable “as indicated by the Contracting Officer,” with both boxes left unmarked. DFARS 252.225-7001, Buy American and Balance of Payments Program, is separately incorporated by reference at the standard clauses section. Please confirm: (a) whether this acquisition is subject to the Trade Agreements Act (i.e., whether the Trade Agreements Certificate applies), or whether it is a Buy American Act/Balance of Payments Program acquisition only; and (b) whether domestic content requirements apply on a component-by-component basis to major equipment items (PV modules, inverters, racking, battery energy storage system, pad-mounted transformer, switchboard, and engine-generators), or only at the end-product level.
response: BMcD considers this an RFI that should be reviewed by USACE as we did not edit this specification.

question:
RFI-11: NDAA Section 154 Covered Battery Restriction
Section 154 of the FY2024 National Defense Authorization Act prohibits the Department of Defense, beginning October 1, 2027, from obligating or expending funds to procure a battery produced by Contemporary Amperex Technology Company (CATL), BYD Company, Envision Energy, EVE Energy Company, Gotion High-Tech Company, Hithium Energy Storage Technology Company, or their successors, where any of these entities assembled or manufactured the final battery or provided a majority of its components. Given that this contract’s period of performance may extend at or beyond that date, please confirm: (a) whether the Government requires contractor certification, at time of proposal or prior to procurement of the BESS, that battery cells and modules are not sourced from any of the entities listed above; (b) whether this requirement applies regardless of when during contract performance the battery procurement or delivery occurs; and (c) whether a waiver process is available or anticipated to be available if a fully compliant, domestically available alternative is not cost-competitive or has an unworkable lead time.
response: BMcD considers this an RFI that should be reviewed by USACE as this requirement listed is coming into effect during construction and would be part of the DIV00 specs.
